mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation that triggers Fed rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of months when CPIAUCSL > 3.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate collapsing consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) signals economic distress that reduces corporate earnings visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0, or directional consistency < 60%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 90.0 indicates manufacturing contraction, signaling recessionary risks that drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of months when INDPRO < 90.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in housing starts (HOUST) indicates expanding consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when HOUST rises, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.0% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases corporate borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average indicates weakening manufacturing, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.
